standard.title: Plan and create artworks that communicate ideas and meaning
standard.description: use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials to plan and create artworks that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create artworks that communicate specific ideas and perspectives using compositional choices and deliberate selection of conventions and materials (AC9AVA4C01). They can generate and select ideas and explain their choices. They have not yet planned artworks systematically, applied aesthetic criteria, or created works that combine digital and analog materials intentionally.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials to plan and create artworks that communicate ideas, perspectives or meaning — making and documenting deliberate choices about how elements serve aesthetic and communicative intentions.

nodes.label: Planning with intention
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan an artwork systematically — generating ideas, identifying visual conventions and processes that will serve their intent, and documenting decisions before making.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a simple plan for an artwork — identify the idea, at least one convention to be used, and one material or process — before beginning the work.
nodes.typical_width: Plan artworks using brainstorming, Viewpoints questions and compositional sketches; identify and document how visual conventions, materials and processes will serve the communicative intent; make and justify choices before making.
wider: Create a logbook comparing analog and digital versions of the same material — document what each can and cannot do and explain which will serve the artwork's intent
Plan an artwork inspired by a text's illustrative approach — analyse how the illustrator's choices serve the narrative, then design your own approach for a different scene
nodes.hinge_reason: Systematic planning is the new demand at Y5-6 compared to Y3-4. Students who skip planning and rely on intuition produce works that can communicate but cannot be refined or defended — subsequent nodes about refining and evaluating choices are inaccessible.

response_modes.reason: Planning is a reasoning process — students need to think forward (what will this produce?) not just backward (why did I make this?). Structured planning prompts build the habit of intentional decision-making before the work begins.

success_criteria: Produces a plan that identifies the idea, at least one convention, and a material or process
Explains how at least one planned choice will serve the communicative intent

nodes.label: Aesthetic choices and material knowledge
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make and explain choices about materials, joining techniques and visual conventions based on the aesthetic qualities they want the artwork to have.
nodes.minimum_width: Make at least one material or process choice based on an aesthetic quality wanted (e.g. durability, texture, translucency, gestural quality) and explain the reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Apply knowledge of material properties to make aesthetic choices (joining techniques, brushstroke qualities, surface effects); compare virtual and analog simulations of the same material; select combinations that communicate intended aesthetic qualities.
wider: Explore how different brushstrokes communicate different meanings — compare long smooth horizontal lines in watercolour wash with textural thick paint strokes; explain what each communicates
Investigate how First Nations Australian artists use specific materials and processes to produce particular visual and cultural effects — with guidance from culturally authoritative resources

response_modes.reason: Material knowledge is built through comparative experience — students who have tried only one material type cannot reason about aesthetic choice. Comparing analog/digital, different paint techniques, and sculptural materials reveals how properties map to aesthetic effects.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The analog/digital comparison and the exploration of brushstroke as expressive choice are particularly rich — students who engage with both develop a more sophisticated understanding of how material is expressive, not just technical.
success_criteria: Makes at least one material or process choice based on an aesthetic quality wanted
Explains the reasoning in terms of what the material or process does — not just personal preference

nodes.label: Creating with coordinated intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create an artwork in which planning, aesthetic choices and communicative intent are coordinated — the work delivers what was intended.
nodes.minimum_width: Create an artwork that realises at least one planned intention; explain how the visual choices made serve that intention.
nodes.typical_width: Create artworks using planned visual conventions, materials and processes; make choices that serve both aesthetic quality and communicative intent; combine multiple elements coherently; include digital and analog combinations where appropriate.
wider: Create an artwork that combines at least one digital and one analog material — document in a logbook and explain how each contributes to the final work
Form modular patterns using grid paper or digital tools (glyphs, pixels, shapes) — remove the grid and transform into a final form such as a poster or printmaking template
Create an artwork in response to a site-specific inspiration — document how the site shaped material and compositional choices

response_modes.reason: Planning, aesthetic judgment and material execution are coordinated here. The integration is not just technical — it is the student demonstrating that what they made matches what they intended.

success_criteria: Creates an artwork that realises at least one planned intention
Explains how at least two visual choices (convention, material, composition) work together to serve the communicative intent
